title: Regional surge squad week digest - 2026-09-21
content:
Week: 2026-09-14 -> 2026-09-20
Owners: Aisha (lead), Ravi (region ops), Marta (preemption), Ethan (cost), Sofia (telemetry)

Summary:
- Focus this week: run a rehearsal for a cross-region surge (eu->na), validate preemptible transition canary, and test reserve-buffer heuristics for edge regions.
- Key signals: queue growth in eu-west3 during peak (daily 17:00-19:00 UTC) with sustained 9k RTQ (ready-to-serve queue) for 30+ min on Tue; p95 tail for model-embed-2 rose to 210ms for that window.
- No customer-facing incidents, internal throttling and fallback policies handled headroom. Canary uncovered two issues: slow pod churn during GPU eviction and KV cache rehydration causing ~200ms extra token latency for first requests after failover.

This week's observations / metrics (raw):
- eu-west3 avg GPU utilization: 78% (spike to 96% during Tue peak)
- na-south1 avg GPU utilization: 34% (we routed 12% of diverted traffic here)
- Preemptible reclaim events: 53 total (most in ap-southeast2), 4 of them overlapped with canary window -> increased evict churn
- RTQ (ready-to-query) high-water: eu-west3 = 9,200; na-south1 = 1,500
- Latency: model-embed-2 p50/p95 = 85ms / 210ms (peak); baseline p95 outside peak = 120ms
- Cold-KV penalty: ~180-230ms for first requests after cache flush (observed in canary)

Huddle notes (timestamps approximate):
- Mon 09:20 — kickoff: discuss surge scenario and objectives. Action: run two simulated surges (traffic replay) Tue & Thu.
- Tue 16:45 — live replay (traffic-mirroring): triggered fallback to model-embed-2-lite in na-south1. Observed: autoscaler took 2m10s to create node pool with GPU attached; workaround: warm pool pre-provisioning reduced time to ~40s in subsequent run.
- Wed 11:00 — telemetry deep-dive: found spike correlating with a background cleanup job (infra-cleanup-107) that temporarily consumed control-plane API quota; tightened rate-limit on cleanup jobs.
- Thu 14:00 — canary for preemptible transition: policy swapped 8 nodes to preemptible; 4 were reclaimed during the 20m window. Outcome: fallback routing succeeded, but KV rehydration and replica scheduling added latency.

Decisions made:
- Add a 12% reserve buffer for eu-west3 for the next 30 days during evening peak (17:00-20:00 UTC). Evaluate after two weeks.
- Implement 'warm-pool' low-cost instances in na-south1 to accept overflow traffic faster (prototype already validated reduces spin-up time to <45s).
- Change autoscaler bootstrap workflow to register a lightweight placeholder service to accept traffic while full GPU node is provisioning (to avoid head-of-line KV cache misses).

Action items (owner — due):
- Aisha — write a short playbook for KV rehydrate mitigation (prefetch + warm-requester) and PR to ops-runbooks (due 2026-09-27).
- Marta — prototype autoscaler change (placeholder service) and run perf bench (due 2026-10-04).
- Ravi — apply temporary 12% reserve in eu-west3; update capacity dashboard (done: 2026-09-22) (owner change note: monitor daily).
- Ethan — cost impact analysis for warm-pool strategy (estimate: +2.1% infra spend if used 25% of peak) (due 2026-09-30).
- Sofia — add KV-first-request telemetry to per-route dashboard; capture cold-hit histograms (due 2026-09-24).

Open questions / risks:
- Preemption frequency in ap-southeast2 remains noisy; do we change region priority for lower SLA workloads? Questions: can we shift some batch routing to ap-southeast2 automatically during non-peak windows? (Marta to investigate).
- Does the warm-pool introduce chargeback complexity for Dedicated customers using reserved capacity? (Finance/Commercial sync required).
- What is acceptable extra latency for first-token penalty in short conversational requests (<6 tokens)? Current penalty (~200ms) may impact UX for some paid tiers. Need product alignment.

Playbook snippets (working draft):
- Surge replay checklist: 1) start mirror at 0.5x; 2) enable fallback route to lite model; 3) monitor RTQ and p95; 4) if RTQ > 7k for >10m, flip reserve + pre-warm pool; 5) escalate to oncall.
- Preemption canary steps: 1) pick a small set of nodes (<=10) in non-critical zone; 2) tag traffic; 3) run reclaimed stress for 20m; 4) capture KV rehydrate histograms and scheduler churn; 5) revert tags.

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Could we prefill KV cache for top-1000 prefixes on warm-pool boot? Maybe use lightweight async rehydrator feeding from global cache snapshot. Tradeoff: memory vs hit rate.
- Consider a transient routing tier for <100ms SLO users — route to regional hot-pool only (guarded by quota).

Links & refs:
- Ops runbook PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-runbooks/pull/218
- Slack thread: #infra-surge-squad pinned convo (see linked_artifacts)
- Jira: JIRA-OPS-1426 (eu-west3 reserve buffer), JIRA-PLT-3379 (autoscaler placeholder service)

Retrospective (quick):
- What went well: warm-pool idea reduced cold-start by ~70% after first validation; fallback routing prevented customer impact.
- What didn't: KV rehydration still causes a noticeable hit; autoscaler bootstrap path needs an intermediate acceptance surface.
- Next week's focus: finish autoscaler prototype, finalize KV mitigation playbook, and run one more full-scale replay targeting the evening peak (Fri 18:00 UTC).

Meeting attendees (who joined the huddles this week):
- Aisha Mendel, Ravi Kapoor, Marta Liu, Ethan Rowe, Sofia García, Jin Park (SRE), Leah Osei (Product), Marco D'Souza (Solutions Eng).

priority: medium-high — customer impact risk if not addressed in 2 weeks
